# Full-text index build and ranked HTTP queries

**Partial run:** all three 10,000-document repeats and one 100,000-document repeat completed. Seeding the second 100,000-document repeat returned HTTP 503; the command exited 1 before its third repeat. No retries were performed. This is not the required complete three-repeat qualification.

Native library: existing FTS build SHA-256 `6533a0f21eb1c8f2aa2b3b9ec8083266467858e16fcef295dbeea610ffe8ddd1`, image `eb791f11027ecc89fa488e38b2fd668529f57d9caec69b671293c573782a41f7`. It includes default encryption support but predates the contract1 patch; these plaintext measurements do not qualify the combined release. The source baseline below additionally includes the benchmark host variable rename from `_FILE` to `_PATH`.

Measured: 2026-10-23T14:07:19Z. Host: mariogk-dev (amd64, 46 logical CPUs). Go: go1.27.3. Commit: `4a20aea2329e4b656095d9e0eed8a7d5cf7ecc01`.

Local two-region test cluster (gru/sjc), Release, client and server on one host; requests target gru. Test-only issuer and temporary database; no production credentials. HTTP serialization, network, server query and response reads are included. This is local API evidence, not OCI capacity. The existing host freezes query deadlines; production timeouts are not measured.

Each size has three independent fresh collections, populated before timing index creation (`kind:text`, `fields:[article.body]`). Documents contain integer `n` and nested `article.body`: 32 words, 129 evenly distributed alphabetic topic tokens, one or four topic occurrences (alternating groups), and orchard filler. Bytes are the summed uncompressed UTF-8 document JSON sizes; HTTP envelopes and index storage are excluded.

One unmeasured disjoint-term query verifies the complete matching ID set and strict frequency ranking. Each repeat measures 128 different search terms exactly once, limit 10, sorted by `$score` descending; no measured query is served from a previous identical query result. Every response must contain only expected distinct IDs and finite descending item scores, with high-frequency matches first. Throughput is sequential closed-loop successful queries / elapsed time, including client correctness checks; it is not maximum concurrent throughput. Latencies exclude those checks. No request retries.

Only completed repeats appear below. A successful command must produce repeats 1–3 for every requested size.
